descriptionChirho: Possessing great physical or military strength; used of persons, nations, or abstract forces that are powerful or prevailing.
Exhibiting intensity, violence, or severity in character, action, or emotional force; used of wrath, treatment, or aggressive disposition.
Applied to a city or stronghold as being well-defended and difficult to conquer; a transferred sense from personal strength to structural impregnability.
Used in construct phrases (fierce-of-face, strong-of-appetite) to describe boldness, insolence, greed, or hardness of demeanor.
